take: Russia’s diesel and gasoil exports crashing to just 80,000 bpd in the first seven days of August is the standout story, tightening an already fuelled global middle-distillate market and underpinning cracks. This supply squeeze comes alongside China’s Q2 crude import drop on higher prices from Strait of Hormuz disruptions, which normalises the demand-side response to the same geopolitical premium. On freight, the intensifying Red Sea attacks and insurers cancelling war risk cover will keep tonne-mile demand elevated for tankers and boxships, whilst Hapag-Lloyd’s 3.5% year-on-year bunker consumption fall highlights efficiency gains against a backdrop of firm fuel prices. The cross-market link is clear: tight gasoil and diesel directly lift VLSFO bunker premiums as refiners maximise distillate yield, and any further Red Sea escalation widens the clean product freight differential. Watch Russian export data over the next 24 hours for confirmation of whether the 80,000 bpd figure is a floor or a precursor to a full ban, which would send European diesel cracks sharply higher.
